claims.claim: Exelon's large-load opportunity is being quality-filtered rather than accepted at face value: Q2 reporting described 11 GW of high-probability load, including 4 GW backed by signed Transmission Security Agreements and about $1 billion of collateral, while the broader prospective data-center pipeline was reduced after filtering speculative projects.

risks.risk: Large-load interconnection demand can remain speculative until collateral, siting, transmission and generation constraints are resolved.

unknowns.unknown: A current issuer-primary Q2 source was not obtained in this Scout pass; Alpha should source-address any numeric underwriting from filings or issuer materials.

claims.claim: The TSA/collateral process is a useful execution test because it converts a headline load queue into financially committed projects; the reduction in the broader pipeline is therefore both a demand haircut and evidence of more disciplined capital screening.

risks.risk: Regulatory affordability constraints and generation/transmission scarcity can delay conversion of committed load into rate-base growth.

unknowns.unknown: Timing and realized returns for individual large-load projects remain uncertain.
